local_checks.invariant: No workflow runs PR-author-controlled code with secrets, a write token, or a trusted-event context (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment).
local_checks.result: All five workflows trigger only on pull_request and push to main. None of them uses pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, or any secrets.* reference (grep over .github/workflows). bash, effver, lint and rust set top-level permissions contents: read. entity-diff.yml is the only workflow with pull-requests: write, and its job condition github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == false (line 20) limits it to same-repo branches, whose authors already hold write access. In that job the PR tree is only parsed by a SHA-pinned action (Ataraxy-Labs/sem/action@04f6990c, sem-version v0.29.1); no PR-controlled script or recipe runs. On pull_request the workflow file itself comes from the PR merge ref, so a PR author who controls justfile, mise.toml, bats or ask-claude gains nothing the workflow file does not already give: a read-only token and no secrets.

local_checks.invariant: Attacker-controlled event fields (branch names, titles, commit messages) never reach a run: script through ${{ }} expression interpolation, and step outputs consumed by later steps are not derived from attacker text.
local_checks.result: The only ${{ }} expression in any run context is effver.yml:33. It passes github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before through env BASE, which is a SHA and not interpolated into the script; the script checks it with git cat-file -e (line 36). rust.yml:47 writes only the constant present=true/false to GITHUB_OUTPUT. The check-effver and effort-floor steps have no id, so no later step reads their outputs. effort-floor output (including the commit subject at effver.just:62) is teed into GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (effver.yml:46-52) inside a code fence that a subject containing ``` can close. On pull_request the author already controls the workflow file and so the summary; on push the commits are already merged. No privilege boundary is crossed.

local_checks.invariant: Mutable build inputs written by lower-trust parties do not reach a privileged or trusted output.
local_checks.result: jdx/mise-action is SHA-pinned (b44d12e7, v5.2.7). mise.toml sets lockfile = true, and mise.lock pins sha256 checksums for bats, hurl, jq, just, shellcheck and usage on all four platforms. Mutable inputs remain: actions/checkout@v7 and Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 are tag-pinned; actionlint comes in through `mise x actionlint@1.7.12` (justfile:34) and has no mise.lock entry; the sem action downloads the v0.29.1 release binary by tag. Every consuming job runs with contents: read and no secrets, and nothing in the repo publishes, releases or deploys. The one write token (entity-diff, pull-requests: write) is reachable only by the upstream maintainers of checkout or sem. That makes these hardening items, not findings. rust.yml steps are all gated on rust/Cargo.toml, which is absent at this commit.

x_hardening: check-effver prints commit-controlled subject, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md heading raw (tools/effver/check-effver:82,97,101,124). Suggested fix: pass printed values through a C0/C1 stripper (e.g. tr -d '\000-\037\177' or printf %q) before printing.

local_checks.invariant: Endpoint-returned content cannot impersonate a user/system turn or alter a deterministic client-side trust decision through the advisor path
local_checks.result: Replies are stored as {role:"assistant", content:.content} with a fixed role (ask-claude call(), after reassemble); user text enters as a typed string content of a role:user entry via jq --rawfile (ask()); $sys is user-supplied only. The only client decisions that read history content are (a) advisor_used in lib/request.jq:58-64, which counts server_tool_use name==advisor after the last role:user entry and lowers max_uses (endpoint-forged blocks can only reduce or zero the client cap; the advisor is a server tool billed and enforced by that same endpoint, so no authority is gained), and (b) the grep for '"advisor_tool_result"' at ask-claude:339, which only adds the advisor beta header to a request going to the same endpoint. Neither decision gates a local capability, credential, or another principal's context. No confirmation, local execution, or secret flows from the advisor path.

local_checks.invariant: Advisor stream and footer rendering (advisor error_code, advisor model) go through safe before reaching the terminal
local_checks.result: Hostile SSE replay with --advisor: advisor_tool_result_error error_code containing ESC ]0;TITLE BEL and ESC[2K printed as '(advisor error: bad]0;TITLE[2Kcode)' with all C0 bytes removed; footer advisor model 'm\u001b[31m' printed as 'm[31m'; non-numeric advisor input_tokens printed as text, not evaluated. Request carried max_uses 3 for a fresh turn. The newline kept by safe in the footer model field (forged second stderr line) belongs to the peer-owned terminal-output safe sanitiser unit and is not claimed here.

x_hardening: lib/event.jq num passes any JSON number and jq 1.7 (sandbox) emits unmodified literals verbatim, so an endpoint can write an arbitrarily long digit string (e.g. request text encoded as decimal bytes) into input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read/cache_write; observed with a 47-digit literal. cents likewise has no length cap on list_cost. This contradicts the README sentence that only a single identifier-like word passes, but crosses no boundary (same endpoint already holds the data; no consumer). Suggested fix: num as `if type == "number" and . >= 0 and . < 1e15 then floor else null end` (arithmetic canonicalises the literal) and cap cents to e.g. {1,15} digits. The pinned jq 1.8.2 literal-preservation behaviour was not run here (sandbox has jq 1.7).

advisor_used (lib/request.jq:58-64) trusts server_tool_use blocks in endpoint-written history; a forged history can only lower the client-side max_uses cap. Harmless today because the cap is a cost guard against the same endpoint, but it should not be reused as a security control.

local_checks.invariant: Severity is separated correctly and the remediation enforces the invariant without moving trust elsewhere.
local_checks.result: Likelihood is low: the attack needs a dot/dash lookalike host that the attacker controls, plus user action while the token is exported. Impact is medium: one server's bearer token is disclosed to another server's operator. Overall low does not exceed impact. The remediation is sound. An injective encoding, or an explicit record of each token's exact host, binds the token to its host. Refusing duplicate folded names or variables closes the case where both hosts are given together. The proposed bash snippet checks a folded name against mcp_vars, so it must run before the current name is appended, and on its own it catches only collisions within one invocation. The record pairs it with the injective-encoding change, which covers the single-URL case.

local_checks.invariant: The FIFO transport cannot be reached or raced by another local principal: pipes live in a private, unpredictable directory that is removed on stop.
local_checks.result: local_mcp_start (ask-claude:597-598) creates the FIFOs inside `mktemp -d` (mode 0700, random name, under umask 077) and opens them only by path from the same process. local_mcp_stop (ask-claude:634-650) runs `rm -rf "$LOCAL_MCP_DIR"` after the group is gone. No other OS user can open, replace or pre-create the pipes. The only leak is the empty directory when mkfifo fails before LOCAL_MCP_PID is set, because stop returns early on an empty PID. That leak is hardening, not a boundary issue.

local_checks.invariant: JSON-RPC correlation: one response cannot be accepted as the answer to a different request in a way that crosses a principal boundary.
local_checks.result: local_mcp_read (ask-claude:566-588) treats any message with `method` as a server request or notification, never as a response, and accepts only `(.id|tostring) == want`. Handshake ids are fixed (`ask-claude-initialize`, `ask-claude-tools-N`) and finish before the first custom call. tools/call reuses the endpoint-chosen custom_tool_use id (ask-claude:674-677). An endpoint that reuses an id, or sends a number and a string that stringify the same, can make a late response to call A (one that timed out at ask-claude:686-688) be accepted as the result of call B. Both calls were already approved by session_confirm (ask-claude:752-755), and the result goes back to that same endpoint. No unapproved call runs and nothing crosses a principal boundary. A non-scalar id (an object) never matches, so the call times out after LOCAL_MCP_TIMEOUT: availability for the invoking user only, which is excluded. A partial line lost to a `read -t` timeout leaves a tail that starts inside a JSON-escaped string, so a crafted tail cannot pass as a valid response.

local_checks.invariant: Descriptor inheritance: the server inherits no ask-claude channel beyond its own stdin and stdout, and later children do not keep the server alive after stop.
local_checks.result: The server is forked (ask-claude:605) before `exec 7>... 8<...` (ask-claude:610), so it does not get fds 7 and 8. Later children (jq, the background stream curl at ask-claude:487, `tail --pid`) do inherit fds 7 and 8. A curl still running at exit can hold the server's stdin open. local_mcp_stop does not depend on EOF: after 1 s it sends SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL, so the server still stops.

local_checks.invariant: Fd inheritance, observed: the server process holds only its FIFO stdin and the stdout/stderr it was given, with no ask-claude state-file descriptors.

local_checks.invariant: Process-group cleanup: at exit, the whole server group is terminated, including a child and a server that ignores EOF and SIGTERM, and the FIFO directory is removed.
local_checks.result: Run: `agent tools` with fake-server, FAKE_MCP_MODE=ignore-eof (the server traps TERM and starts `sleep 300`). ask-claude exited 0. local_checks.invariant: Stale handle: local_mcp_alive and the group kill target only the server's group. The comment at ask-claude:652-653 says this holds because the exited sh stays a zombie until local_mcp_stop waits on it.
local_checks.result: That premise is false. I started a server that exits right after the handshake; 1 s later ps showed no entry, zombie or otherwise, for LOCAL_MCP_PID, because bash's SIGCHLD handler had already reaped the job. From that point LOCAL_MCP_PID names a free pid. local_mcp_alive matches any running process whose pgid equals that number. The harness simulated reuse with a shimmed ps (not real pid wraparound): local_mcp_alive returned true, so local_mcp_stop would send TERM and then KILL to `-$pid`. This needs the server to die early and the same pid to be reused as a same-user group leader before exit. No lower-trust principal controls pid reuse, and the signal can only reach same-uid processes. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

x_hardening: ask-claude:605 `sh -c "$cmd"` passes the whole environment to the local MCP server, including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN and ASK_CLAUDE_MCP_TOKEN_* (seen locally in check1-reap-fds-env.txt). Suggested change: start the server with `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u GITHUB_TOKEN ...` (and the per-host MCP token variables), or with an allowlisted environment, as defense in depth against accidental secret logging by third-party servers.

ask-claude:634-655 stale process-group handle: bash reaps the background job when it exits, so after an early server exit LOCAL_MCP_PID can be reused, and local_mcp_alive plus `kill -- -$LOCAL_MCP_PID` could then signal an unrelated same-user process group at exit. The code comment's zombie premise is wrong (verified locally). Suggested change: in local_mcp_stop, first check `jobs -p`, or check whether `wait -n`/`kill -0` still sees the job as running. Alternatively, record the server's start time (`ps -o lstart= -p`) at start and confirm it before signalling. Regression test: a server that exits after the handshake, then a ps shim reporting that pgid, and assert that stop sends no signal.
